standard_prerequisites.name: A pseudo-coherent object over a ring is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, and pseudo-coherence is preserved under a surjection with locally nilpotent kernel when the target object is pseudo-coherent
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the representative over the first ring and propagates pseudo-coherence to every member of the system.

standard_prerequisites.name: Maps in the derived category between the members of the system may be lifted to maps of complexes of finite free modules inducing isomorphisms after reduction to the previous ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Builds the system of complexes whose limit represents the derived limit.

standard_prerequisites.name: The derived limit of a system of complexes is represented by the limit of the complexes, and the limit of finite free modules of bounded rank is again finite free of that rank
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the limit complex is a bounded above complex of finite free modules, which gives pseudo-coherence and the final assertion.

core_obligations: Represent the first object by a bounded above complex of finite free modules over the first ring, using the definition of pseudo-coherence, and conclude from the nilpotent kernel statement that every object of the system is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 28353-28359).

Construct by induction complexes of finite free modules over each ring representing the corresponding object, together with maps between them representing the given maps, such that the reductions modulo the kernels are isomorphisms of complexes (proof lines 28359-28365).

Use the representation of the derived limit by the limit of the system of complexes, whose terms are the limits of the finite free modules of bounded rank and hence finite free of the same ranks, to conclude that the derived limit is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 28365-28372).

Read off the second assertion: the derived tensor product of the limit with any member of the system is represented by the corresponding complex of the system, because the reductions of the limit complex are those complexes (proof lines 28372-28374).
proof_roadmap: Represent the first object and propagate pseudo-coherence along the system (proof lines 28353-28359).
Lift the system to complexes of finite free modules with strict reductions (proof lines 28359-28365).
Identify the derived limit with the limit complex of finite free modules and conclude both assertions (proof lines 28365-28374).
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns an inverse system of rings with surjective transition maps having locally nilpotent kernels, objects over each ring compatible under reduction, and asks that the derived limit be pseudo-coherent and be recovered by reduction (statement lines 28335-28351). The proof represents the first object by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, propagates pseudo-coherence along the system through the nilpotent kernel statement, lifts the system to complexes of finite free modules whose reductions are isomorphisms of complexes, and then identifies the derived limit with the limit complex, whose terms are finite free of the same bounded ranks (proof lines 28353-28374). The strictness of the reductions is what makes the limit complex computable and hence pseudo-coherent. The counted span refers five times, four times to results of this chapter and once to a remark of this chapter accompanying the computation of derived limits, all carried as navigation stubs.
